# nonBoolean

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is **not** a boolean.</link-summary>

<web-summary>nonBoolean() — Checks whether a value is **not** a boolean. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.1.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function nonBoolean<T>(value: T | boolean): value is T;
```

`nonBoolean(value)` is the same test as `!isBoolean(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.

Only the two primitives pass. `new Boolean(false)` is an object, and the strings `"true"` and `"false"` are strings.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type           | Description         |
| :-------- | :------------- | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `T \| boolean` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is not a boolean; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `value` to `T` inside the branch.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
nonBoolean("true"); // => true
nonBoolean(1); // => true
nonBoolean(null); // => true
nonBoolean(true); // => false
nonBoolean(false); // => false
```
